A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same discrepancy-gated VLA work despite the changed title and terminology. The main texts, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support comparison, with substantial experimental content directly matching across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original LIBERO, RoboCasa, Franka, and humanoid experiments, together with perturbation tests and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulation and robot results and adds real-world tasks, component ablations, and reliability diagnostics.

M1.justification: The centroid-based discrepancy, exponential gate, stopped-gate loss weighting, and linear residual already exist in v1. v2 incorporates the previously described previous-chunk gate into the initialization of iterative refinement, whereas v1's iterative Algorithm 2 starts from ungated features. It also specifies first-action execution and replanning. The sorting-free centroid formula is mathematically equivalent to the earlier construction.

E1.justification: v2 retains LIBERO, RoboCasa, the four Franka tasks, and humanoid clean-up. Table 6 and Figure 8 add Arrange-Flower and Bimanual Handover under standard and visually shifted conditions, providing a limited extension to the existing real-world manipulation coverage.

E2.justification: v2 removes π0-Fast from the LIBERO comparison; v1 Table 1 reported its 85.5% average. v2 Table 7 adds loss-reweighting-only and learned-MLP-gate controls. The other principal benchmark comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: The reported residual strength changes from 0.4 to 0.1. FR3 execution changes from 20 Hz commands and open-loop chunks to first-action replanning at 10 Hz with 50 Hz interpolation. Appendix B states 30k training steps across experiments, replacing v1's humanoid-specific 20k. v2 consistently specifies three refinement rounds where v1 gives conflicting defaults, and introduces failure-prediction AUROC diagnostics. These are reported setting changes, without evidence establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 Table 7 adds targeted tests separating loss reweighting from residual refinement and comparing transport gating with a learned MLP gate. New Table 8 relates discrepancy and gate values to rollout success/failure, reports failure-prediction AUROC, and examines gains for high-discrepancy states. These directly investigate the central reliability mechanism. The earlier refinement, projection-budget, and temperature/residual sweeps are largely retained.

E5.justification: v2 Table 8 newly reports interquartile ranges for discrepancy and gate values on Perturb-OOD, separated by success and failure. v1 reports batch variability in its training-cost plot but lacks these distributional summaries. Neither version reports multiple training seeds, confidence intervals for benchmark success, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The principal simulation scores and humanoid clean-up scores are retained, but v2 adds substantial results: 97.3% and 97.5% LIBERO averages for the loss-only and MLP controls, failure AUROCs of 0.82/0.84, and new visual-shift task outcomes. Franka entries also change: DiG Stack-Bowls sub-task/whole-task success changes from 62/48 to 65/50. These are added or revised reports, not established same-setting improvements across versions.

T1.justification: v1's gated-descent, residual-improvement, and fixed-gate contraction theorems, supporting assumptions, and Appendix A proofs are removed. v2 introduces a Gaussian-residual/chi-square proposition motivating the exponential gate and a mixture-reweighting theorem bounding shortcut mass and risk, with new proofs. The mathematical foundation is substantially replaced.

C1.justification: v1 foregrounds geometric regularization and guarantees of objective decrease and refinement convergence. v2 foregrounds transport discrepancy as an internal, per-step reliability signal and replaces the theoretical contribution with local statistical motivation and shortcut-mixture suppression. It explicitly declines a contraction guarantee for the implemented loop. The broad empirical robustness claim is retained.

C2.justification: v2 develops the decodable-region interpretation and adds specific limitations involving indistinguishable action centroids, physically infeasible but feature-compatible actions, and inadequate recovery from unsupported observations. It interprets refinement through damping rather than a contraction guarantee and discusses costs for faster control loops. v1's limitations concerning bounded features, batch composition, and extension beyond demonstrated actions are removed.

D1.justification: v2 documents reuse of the action expert's projector, gradient routing, freezing schedules, action horizon 16, feature dimension 1024, gate floor 0.05, evaluation counts, and measured runtime overhead. Appendix B consolidates settings and reports A800 training hardware instead of A100. Conversely, v1's explicit learning rate, cosine schedule, spectral-normalization bound, perturbation coefficients, and real-robot demonstration counts disappear. These omissions do not establish that the underlying procedures were removed.

R1.justification: Related work adds VIPA-VLA, Being-H0.5, and several predictive/world-model VLA references, including DreamVLA and VLA-JEPA, while removing FAST. Positioning emphasizes the lack of internal reliability estimates. The main VLA, robustness, and optimal-transport context, including the distinction from OT-CFM, remains intact.

P1.justification: The title changes and DiG-Flow becomes DiG, accompanied by extensive rewriting of the abstract, introduction, method, and experimental interpretation. The standalone theoretical-analysis section is replaced by theory integrated into the method, experimental subsections are consolidated, and the appendices are reorganized around new proofs and hyperparameters.

P2.justification: v2 merges the clean and perturbed Franka tables, transposes and combines the discrepancy/gating ablation tables, and adds hardware, reliability, and hyperparameter tables. Robot photographs and rollout panels are reorganized, visual-shift examples are added, and the existing refinement and training-cost plots become a combined figure. These are extensive display changes beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: The targeted controls and success/failure diagnostics in v2 Tables 7–8 provide more direct support for the reliability claim, while withdrawing the implemented-loop contraction claim improves qualification. Added implementation details also help reproducibility. These gains are tempered by unresolved inconsistencies: Figure 10 still tests λ = 0.2–0.6 while the text and Appendix B recommend 0.1, earlier reproduction details disappear, and retained headline scores accompany revised settings without explaining reruns. The evidence supports a limited overall improvement.
